hints.title: Exponential Path Search Obstacle
hints.text: Exploring paths from every cell with naive recursion recomputes overlapping paths exponentially many times, timing out on large grids. Because each step in a path must strictly increase in cell value, why are cycles naturally impossible?

hints.title: Implicit DAG and Subproblem Caching
hints.text: Because values strictly increase along any valid path, the grid forms a directed acyclic graph where the longest path starting at any cell can be solved as an independent subproblem and memoized.

hints.title: Neighbor Exploration and Memoization
hints.text: Define a recursive function returning the longest path starting at cell (r, c). For each of its four neighbors with strictly larger values, recursively obtain their longest paths and take one plus their maximum, defaulting to one if no neighbor is larger. Memoize each cell and return the maximum across all cells.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: DFS with memoization on Directed Acyclic Graph formed by strictly increasing cell values.

solutions.approach: Implicit DAG on 2D Matrix (Strict Ordering eliminates cycles)
